A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Glauber Generative Model research. All 29 pages of each version, including Appendices A–J, are available and readable; text comparison and visual inspection support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-generation perplexities, image-generation FID scores, and qualitative generation and infilling results in Tables 1–2, figures, and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports revised GGM scores, an additional MDLM comparison, and replacement language and image generations.

M1.justification: Appendix G adapts Algorithm A3 from a constant noise distribution to time-varying retention probabilities, changing its inputs, cumulative probability calculation, and final noise draw. This is a limited extension of the direct forward sampler; the architecture, binary-classification objective, and main reverse and conditional procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OpenWebText language generation, CelebA-HQ and FFHQ image generation, and text/image infilling. Replacement illustrative examples retain these tasks. The new OpenWebText2 mention explains Plaid’s training background rather than introducing another evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MDLM as an evaluated language-generation comparator. The GPT2, BERT/Gibbs, Plaid, and SEDD comparisons remain, and Table 2 retains its image-generation comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix H retunes existing experiments: language training changes from 1.96M steps with a 10M-step cosine schedule to 2M steps with a 2M-step schedule, and peak/final learning rates change from 5e-5/5e-8 to 1e-4/1e-6. FFHQ training increases from 2.44M to 3M steps, with decay extended from 2M to 3M. MDLM uses 170M parameters and 1000 sampling steps. Metrics, generation lengths, and evaluation sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix J.1 replaces the four illustrative text-infilling outputs and three corresponding prompts, revising the qualitative evidence for prefix/suffix consistency. The image-masking demonstrations, nearest-neighbor analysis, and design of the BERT sampling-step comparison are retained; no new systematic ablation or robustness study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The evaluation sample counts do not constitute repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces GGM perplexities 22.3/22.7/20.6 with 19.5/19.9/18.0 under GPT2-large/GPT2-xl/GPT-Neo evaluation and adds MDLM values 44.2/45.4/40.9. Table 2 changes FFHQ FID from 14.2 to 12.5 while retaining CelebA-HQ FID 9.8. These accompany revised training settings, not a controlled same-setting gain. Figure 2a is updated, and FFHQ and language samples are replaced; the principal findings remain similar.

T1.justification: Appendix G relaxes the constant-distribution assumption to constant token-noise proportions with time-varying retention probabilities and revises the associated derivation. It also corrects the prose’s replacement draw to the distribution conditioned on vocabulary tokens. Lemmas 1–3 and their proofs remain unchanged. The generalized overwrite probability still uses 1-product(1-Pi_s(phi)), inconsistent with Equation 1’s implied 1-product(Pi_s(phi)); the tested retention probability of 0.5 masks this discrepancy.

C1.justification: Section 1.2 drops the assertion that competing multi-token methods necessarily require sequence-to-sequence models; Remark 1 instead contrasts single-token with all-token prediction. This narrows one claimed distinction. The central reduction, discrete-language-diffusion performance, image-generation, and zero-shot infilling claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly contextualizes GGM’s competitiveness with Plaid through its smaller training corpus, OpenWebText versus OpenWebText2. Appendix H removes the stated convergence benefit of sampling multiple timesteps per example. The explanations involving image tokenizers, remaining state-of-the-art gaps, and FID limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds MDLM implementation and license information and revises training hyperparameters. It replaces the image-batch description of 512 examples times four timesteps with a batch size of 2048, leaving the decomposition unspecified. The rare-token suppression disclosure is removed, without establishing whether the heuristic was abandoned. Appendix J.2 newly specifies top-p 0.9 for its unconditional examples.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gao et al.’s The Pile reference for the OpenWebText2 discussion and Sahoo et al.’s masked diffusion language model reference for MDLM. The existing references are retained, and the related-work survey is otherwise substantively stable. The sequence-to-sequence comparison is also narrowed.

P1.justification: There are localized wording changes in the contributions, method comparison, results discussion, and Appendices G/H, plus a sampling-description sentence in Appendix J.2. The section organization and overall narrative remain stable; replacement generated passages are experimental outputs rather than extensive rewriting of the exposition.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an MDLM row and explicit length/step entries for GPT2. Figure 2a is redrawn with a horizontal GGM reference line, and the FFHQ grids in Figures 2b and 8 contain replacement images. Figures 2–3 and Table 2 move within the results pages. The overall visual design and other figure contents remain stable.

improvement.justification: The added MDLM comparison and clearer disclosures about Plaid’s training corpus and qualitative sampling modestly improve evidence and transparency. Lower GGM scores accompany revised training and do not establish a controlled version-to-version gain. Some inference detail is lost, and Appendix G’s attempted generalization retains a probability error. These limit the improvement, but the core proofs and experimentally used retention probability of 0.5 are unaffected.
